edict-of-milan: Emperors Constantine and Licinius grant religious tolerance across the Roman Empire, ending the persecution of Christians.
fall-of-constantinople: Ottoman Sultan Mehmed II takes the city, ending the Byzantine Empire after more than a thousand years.
luthers-95-theses: Martin Luther's challenge to the Catholic Church in Wittenberg starts the Protestant Reformation.
diet-of-worms: Ordered to recant before Emperor Charles V, Luther refuses and is declared an outlaw.
dutch-east-india-company-voc-founded: Often called the first multinational company, and the first to issue shares traded on a stock exchange.
industrial-revolution: Steam power, factories and railways transform Britain first, then Europe and North America.
archduke-franz-ferdinand-assassinated: The heir to Austria-Hungary's throne is shot in Sarajevo. Within six weeks Europe is at war.
eclipse-confirms-relativity: Arthur Eddington's expedition measures starlight bending around the Sun during a solar eclipse, as relativity predicted. Einstein becomes world-famous overnight.
